content.thinking:
I need to structure the root cause, executive summary, and assumptions carefully, treating the given impact figures as measured facts from the shop rather than something I calculated myself, and avoiding introducing any new numbers of my own.

For assumptions, I should note the unknowns: who disabled the flag, whether it coincided with a deploy, which users were affected, and that the recovery is correlated with the revert but not proven causal.

assumptions: The elapsed time the automated responder held the incident (about a minute) reflects response speed, not how long the service was degraded; the outage window is taken from the metrics as 21:41-21:47 UTC.
Who or what turned off legacy-checkout-fallback, and why, was not established during the incident - only that the flag provider's history shows one recent change to it.

Causation between the flag flip and the errors is inferred from exact timing correlation, the ZeroDivisionError stack location, and the absence of any deploy or config change in the window; it was not proven by reproduction.

Recovery is attributed to reverting the flag because the service returned to baseline shortly after the revert; no other remediation was applied, but this is correlation rather than a controlled test.
Impact is assumed limited to account-page rendering, since all error log lines in the window reference that path; other endpoints were not separately verified.
The pre-incident errors (ClientDisconnected) are treated as normal background noise unrelated to this incident.
Log lines reviewed covered only the eight minutes before the alert and appear sampled rather than exhaustive, so the log excerpt is not a complete count of failures.
The proposed pull request is assumed to address the divide-by-zero defect but had not been reviewed or merged at the time of writing.
input.executive_summary: For roughly six minutes on 28 September 2026, from 21:41 to 21:47 UTC, a large share of visits to the online shop's account page failed with an error instead of loading. Other parts of the shop were not affected, and the failures were immediate errors rather than slow or partial pages, so no orders or account data were corrupted. The cause was a setting that had been switched off, which pushed account-page traffic down an untested path in the software that could not handle it. Automated response detected the problem, identified the setting change as the likely cause, and switched it back on; the page returned to its normal error levels and stayed there. A draft code change has been opened to fix the underlying defect so the same setting can be turned off safely in future. The measured impact figures for this window are recorded with the incident metrics and are not restated here.
input.root_cause: At 21:41 UTC the feature flag `legacy-checkout-fallback` flipped from on to off for essentially all traffic on io-shop, which routed account-page requests into a code path in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47` that divides by zero when the fallback is not in use, raising ZeroDivisionError on a large share of those requests. No deploy or config change landed in the window; the error rate stepped up exactly with the flag transition and returned to baseline once the flag was set back on.
